absent: Behavior and severity of usercopy_abort and overlap and alias helpers, including fault versus log semantics.
Stack classification logic and stack pointer handling behind check_stack_object outcomes.
Slab checker criteria and predicates for kernel map, virtual allocation, direct map validity and page size.
Default and lifetime of enable_checks and validate_usercopy_range and option string syntax.
Userfault context lifecycle, change lock ordering, concurrent change protocol, and huge page fill path.
Numeric values and ABI stability of fill modes, mapping flags, page markers and error mappings.
Non anonymous operation vectors including file cache add and remove, no allocation lookup, and zero page policy.
Page table allocation, locking, cache and TLB maintenance, and reverse mapping and counter accounting details.

findings.text: Hardened usercopy range validator visible outside its translation unit. It accepts a kernel address with byte count and copy direction and either returns quietly or terminates the copy path on policy breach, treating zero length as unconditionally valid.

Destination mapping validator visible outside its translation unit. It reports whether a proposed fill end remains inside the supplied mapping and whether that mapping carries an active userfault registration.

Mapping lookup plus anonymous preparation helper visible outside its translation unit. It expects address space protection by the caller and yields either a mapping pointer or an encoded error for missing entries and failed anonymous setup.

Boot time configuration entries for hardened usercopy. One parses a boolean option string with a warning on malformed input, the other enables or disables a global validation branch according to the parsed flag.

Bogus address policy treats arithmetic overflow past the top of the address space as invalid and treats null or zero allocation origins as invalid. Either breach aborts the copy with direction preserved for diagnostics.

Kernel image exposure policy forbids user copies overlapping the linked kernel text extent and, where the architecture provides a distinct linear alias of that extent, forbids overlap with the alias as well. A single mapping terminates early without alias work.

Heap containment policy varies by backing kind. Special kernel mappings are bounded to a single page remainder, virtual allocations require an existing area and containment within it when faults are allowed, valid direct mapped pages delegate slab cases to the allocator checker and compound cases to the compound size remainder, while other pages are left unchecked.

Hardened validation proceeds as a short decision chain from trivial acceptance through address sanity and stack classification to heap and image checks. Stack contained objects judged good exit immediately, non stack objects continue onward, and unrecognized stack classifications abort.

Fill operation cursor bundling the userfault context with requested source base, destination base, length and behavior flags, plus resolved destination mapping, per page source and destination cursors, and cached middle level table entry for the current page. Members are ctx, src_start, dst_start, len, flags, vma, src_addr, dst_addr and pmd.

Retry validation snapshot capturing the operations vector, referenced file, masked mapping flags and start offset used to detect concurrent mapping changes across a lock drop. Members are ops, file, flags and pgoff.

Anonymous mappings accept userfault handling except in minor mode, allocate movable high user folios with memory accounting and cleanup on accounting failure, and are selected through a dedicated operations vector while other mappings defer to their own file operations vector when present.

Destination acceptance requires the fill end to stay within the candidate mapping and requires an active userfault registration on that mapping, preserving the write permission check performed at registration time.

Lookup for fill preparation asserts address space protection, resolves the mapping containing the destination, treats absence as a not found condition, and prepares anonymous infrastructure for private mappings with allocation failure reported as out of memory.

First locking variant favors lightweight acquisition by attempting a read protected lookup that private mappings may only use when anonymous infrastructure already exists, otherwise falling back to address space read protection with mapping preparation and conversion to a mapping read hold. Success is coupled with destination validation and release occurs through the mapping read release.

Second locking variant always holds address space read protection across lookup, preparation and destination validation, returning with that protection held on success and releasing it on failure or through a dedicated unlock that derives the address space from the mapping.

Fill session establishment pairs mapping acquisition with a registration change read hold and a concurrent change sequence check that forces retry if mappings are mutating. Teardown releases the change hold before releasing the mapping hold and clears the cached mapping.

After acquisition the destination mapping must not be an inconsistent anonymous shared combination, write protect fills require write protect registration, huge table mappings bypass further operation checks, and other mappings require a suitable operations vector with continuation mode additionally requiring a no allocation lookup method.

Middle table preparation walks the top levels allocating missing intermediates, ensures a page table exists for an empty entry, then enforces that the entry is present, non leaf and well formed, treating huge or transitional states as already present and malformed entries as faulty.

File backed destinations are bounded by current file size expressed in pages. Mappings without a file never exceed, while indexed positions at or beyond the rounded up size are treated as faulty during installation.

Atomic page installation derives writability from mapping permissions narrowed for cached pages in private mappings, optionally marks write protected entries, permits only empty or userfault marker destinations, attaches reverse mappings and usage accounting appropriate to cached versus new anonymous pages, then publishes the entry and updates the cache without invalidation.

In lock user copying maps the destination folio locally and suppresses faults around the user read to avoid address space lock recursion deadlocks, reporting a fault on short copy and flushing caches on success before unmapping.

Retry comparison tracks masked userfault and sharing flags plus the effective operations vector and file identity with start offset, holding a file reference while the lock is dropped. Any flag, vector, anonymity, file, inode or offset divergence signals that the mapping changed underneath.

Atomic fill follows acquire, validate, establish, allocate, transfer and publish with locked copy fast path and unlocked retry slow path. Missing operation support, allocation failure, transfer failure, file cache insertion failure and install contention each release resources appropriately and propagate distinct errors, with private copy fills forced through anonymous allocation.

Zeroing chooses between allocated folio and shared zero page strategies. Shared mappings or address spaces forbidding the zero page use an allocated zeroed folio through the generic path, while other cases install a special zero entry only onto an empty destination with size validation.

Continuation resolves an already present file folio without allocation, rejects missing entries as faults and poisoned pages as input output errors, then installs through the common installer with proper unlock and reference release on all paths.

Poisoning installs a poison marker only onto a strictly empty destination with size validation, refusing to overwrite any present entry or existing marker, and publishes without invalidation on success.

Dropping address and mapping locks for unbounded user copying exposes the mapping and table entry to concurrent modification, so the implementation snapshots identity before the drop and revalidates mapping, flags, operations and table state after reacquisition, treating divergence as retryable.

Huge and transitional middle table states are treated strictly as conflicts rather than overwritten, and page table publication assumes a prior non present state that needs no invalidation, making stale table reuse or concurrent huge promotion a source of spurious already present failures if not retried at a higher level.

Nested address space read acquisition across processes can deadlock against concurrent writers, so fault suppression confines the in lock user access to a bounded attempt and defers the full copy until after locks are released.
